title: Fourier Series
short: Write a periodic function as a sum of sines and cosines.
trouble: Students use the wrong interval length in the coefficient formulas.

blocks.html: Taylor series build a function from powers of $x$. Fourier series build a periodic function from sines and cosines, the eigenfunctions of the previous lesson. They describe sound, heat and signals, and they solve the heat and wave equations. Computing coefficients uses integration by parts again and again.

For $f$ with period $2L$, $$f(x) \sim \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_n\cos\frac{n\pi x}{L} + b_n\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right),$$ $$a_n = \frac{1}{L}\int_{-L}^{L} f(x)\cos\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx,$$ $$b_n = \frac{1}{L}\int_{-L}^{L} f(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx.$$ Here $L$ is half the period. If $f$ is odd, every $a_n = 0$; if $f$ is even, every $b_n = 0$. At a jump, the series converges to the average of the two one-sided values.

The building blocks are orthogonal on $[-L, L]$. Using $\cos A\cos B$ $= \frac{1}{2}\left(\cos(A - B) + \cos(A + B)\right)$, the integral $\int_{-L}^{L} \cos\frac{m\pi x}{L}\cos\frac{n\pi x}{L}\,dx$ is a sum of cosines over whole periods, so it is 0 when $m \ne n$ and $L$ when $m = n \ge 1$. The same holds for sines, and every sine-cosine product integrates to 0. Now multiply the series by $\cos\frac{m\pi x}{L}$ and integrate: every term dies except $a_m\cdot L$, which gives the formula for $a_m$. For $n = 0$, $\int_{-L}^{L} 1\,dx = 2L$, which is why the constant term is written $\frac{a_0}{2}$: then one formula covers every $a_n$.

blocks.title: A square wave
blocks.q: Find the Fourier series of $f = -1$ on $(-\pi, 0)$ and $f = 1$ on $(0, \pi)$, period $2\pi$.
steps: $\cos n\pi = (-1)^{n}$: $b_n = \frac{4}{n\pi}$ for odd $n$ and 0 for even $n$.

blocks.title: A sawtooth
steps: $L = 1$ and $f$ is odd, so $b_n = 2\int_0^{1} x\sin n\pi x\,dx$.
By parts: $\int_0^{1} x\sin n\pi x\,dx$ $= \left[-\frac{x\cos n\pi x}{n\pi}\right]_0^{1}$ $+ \frac{1}{n\pi}\int_0^{1}\cos n\pi x\,dx$ $= -\frac{(-1)^{n}}{n\pi} + 0$.

blocks.title: An even function
blocks.q: Find the series of $f(x) = x^{2}$ on $(-\pi, \pi)$.
steps: Integrating by parts twice, $a_n = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi} x^{2}\cos nx\,dx$ $= \frac{4(-1)^{n}}{n^{2}}$.

blocks.html: Using the wrong interval length. $L$ is half the period: for period $2\pi$, $L = \pi$, and for period 6, $L = 3$. The factor in front is $\frac{1}{L}$ (or $\frac{2}{L}$ over half the interval for odd or even functions), and the same $L$ appears inside $\frac{n\pi x}{L}$. Using $\frac{1}{2L}$, or $\frac{1}{\pi}$ when the period is not $2\pi$, scales every coefficient wrongly.

blocks.name: de-fourier
blocks.cap: Partial sums of the square wave's series. Add terms: the sum hugs the square wave more closely, passes through the midpoint 0 at each jump, and keeps a small overshoot right next to each jump (the Gibbs phenomenon, about 9% of the jump).

blocks.name: seriespartial
blocks.cap: The square wave's series at $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$, where $\sin nx$ is $1, 0, -1, 0, \dots$: the terms are $\frac{4}{\pi}\left(1 - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} - \dots\right)$, and the partial sums settle on $f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 1$.
